scope: Shipped panel and imported modules served unchanged from in-memory byte snapshot. Fake chrome APIs, generated supported Markdown, no provider/native/browser-wide benchmark. Only completed articles get a fixture class. Current streaming article remains uncontained.

method.trialOrder: For each of 4/100 exchanges and each candidate: baseline, candidate, candidate, baseline, baseline, candidate. Three baseline and three candidate measurements per comparison. One process; fresh page per trial; no parallel trials.
method.transcript: Each exchange goes through actual composer submit, fake chat port, delta and complete. 4 and 100 exchanges retain 8 and 200 articles. Supported headings, emphasis, links, paragraphs, lists, quote, code fence. No transcript truncation or DOM virtualization. Stored fixture session data is in memory only.
method.stream: 20 incoming deltas, each containing one formatted paragraph, separated by two animation frames. CDP Performance counters bracket stream after new send settles. Current streaming article is never marked completed.
method.resize: 8 alternating 360/400px viewport changes, two animation frames per step. Timings are renderer layout/style durations, not elapsed browsing speed.

units.LayoutDuration: seconds of CDP renderer layout work; summary converts to ms
units.RecalcStyleDuration: seconds of CDP renderer style recalculation; summary converts to ms
units.JSHeapUsedSize: V8 used heap bytes at sampling time; no forced GC; excludes native memory
units.Nodes: CDP node counter includes more than attached transcript nodes; GC timing can differ

method.animationCaveat: Initial run waited two frames after fixture construction but did not explicitly wait for entry animation. It may overlap the beginning of streaming trials. Long-transcript follow-up waited 160ms before construction and confirmed initial overflow was transient. Final reproducible harness includes that settling wait; raw historical timing run is retained, not represented as a rerun of the revised harness.
noClaims: No physical RAM measurement or RSS/physical-footprint inference. Audited native probe not invoked.
No browser-wide CPU, memory, energy or browsing-speed claim.
No cold-load or transcript construction timing claim.
No elimination of retained transcript, message map, JS text or DOM. ES-01 ownership growth remains.

featureAssessment.content: All original articles remain attached. Both candidates retained all tokens across selection spanning the entire transcript. Follow-up full selected-text SHA256 is identical across baseline and both candidates at 320 and 400px. Selection serialization approximates copy text; no clipboard access or real copy/paste test.
featureAssessment.markdown: All 18 behavior cases match exact shipped final renderer innerHTML including headings, code and lists.
featureAssessment.scrolling: Top/middle/bottom article scrollIntoView succeeds for every variant. Reader target top stays unchanged during incoming deltas. Bottom-following and final bottom gap are zero once explicitly positioned at bottom. Initial completed-restore-like construction does not stay at bottom in baseline either, because finish performs final full render after last send scroll; not classified as candidate regression.
featureAssessment.resize: Both candidates keep the selected middle target visible on long-conversation width changes; baseline target moves out of view. The position is not pixel-identical after resize even with candidates. Short-case relative positions match baseline. Native content-size estimates change the scrollbar extent; e.g. initial auto600 long extent differs substantially from baseline. This is not proof that arbitrary scrollbar dragging or every resize preserves location.
featureAssessment.find: window.find finds and selects unique old off-screen text in all 18 cases. It does not scroll/reveal the match in this headless Chrome nested scroller, including unchanged baseline. Native browser Find UI was not exercised. Match reachability passes; automatic reveal acceptance remains unverified. Do not claim full find-in-page acceptance.
featureAssessment.keyboard: Off-screen last transcript link can receive focus and is revealed; Tab leaves the link to a focusable control; keyboard model menu Escape returns focus. Full sequential traversal of every link and screen-reader browse navigation were not performed.
featureAssessment.accessibility: Conversation main, labeled live log, and all named articles remain exposed. Candidate snapshots omit off-screen descendant headings/links/lists while baseline exposes them; a focused last off-screen link is then meaningfully exposed in follow-up. Raw AX counts alone do not establish a regression. VoiceOver reading order, browse navigation of skipped text and live announcements were not exercised, so equivalent accessibility is not proven.
featureAssessment.views: 320px reduced motion and 400px ordinary view tested, with resize to opposite width and 620px height. Reduced-motion cases have zero running animations at final capture. Settled long follow-up has no horizontal page overflow in any variant. Initial overflow observations are retained as transient entry-animation observations, not attributed to containment.
featureAssessment.errors: No page errors or fixture external requests in either run.

priorEvidence.ES01: Initial extension-services audit confirms 200 live messages/map entries/articles after 100 exchanges vs 60 persisted. It measures ownership/count growth, not a native memory leak. Native off-screen rendering leaves those ownership structures intact.
priorEvidence.currentVerification: Current README/verification claim incremental streaming stable-block reuse, final safe full rendering, reader-position/bottom-following checks and 320/400px reduced-motion coverage. They explicitly leave native/browser-wide performance unmeasured. This experiment uses those current source bytes and does not retest provider/native integration.

documentation.finding: Auto is intended to preserve find/tab/focus/selection availability; selection/focus can force relevance. Draft permits omission of skipped AX contents when required to avoid revealing assistive-technology timing. Therefore tree-size differences are not sufficient evidence of a user regression.
Describes off-screen layout/paint skipping. These are draft expectations, not a guarantee of behavior in this browser.

documentation.status: 404 from documentation fetch; not used as evidence

recommendation.appliesTo: Adopting either tested CSS variant as a general panel resource optimization
recommendation.reason: The resize-only layout benefit is real within this component fixture, but streaming layout medians worsen in all four comparisons and no heap reduction is established. More importantly, full find reveal and assistive reading reachability are unresolved. This does not meet the required unchanged-behavior acceptance gate. No production change authorized or implemented.
recommendation.qualifiedAnswer: Browser-native skipping can reduce repeated width-change layout work while retaining DOM/text, but this bounded experiment does not establish a safe overall resource improvement. It cannot fix ES-01 live text/map/DOM retention.
recommendation.furtherEvidenceIfRevisited: Only revisit for a measured resize-heavy workload with explicit scroll extent/location acceptance and native Find plus VoiceOver browse/live-log tests. No broad rewrite is warranted from these data.

limitations: One installed headless Google Chrome 156 build on macOS arm64, not native Breezer extension integration.
Three samples per comparison; no statistical population inference. Initial animation overlap and scheduler noise limit small streaming differences.
Synthetic repetitive supported Markdown; ordinary 4-exchange case included, but user content and prolonged interactive sessions vary.
No real provider, APIs, login, profile, Keychain, app build, install, PC, SSH, publication, dependency changes or native helper benchmark.
Completion marking is fixture-owned, outside measured streaming segment; a production mechanism and its runtime overhead were not implemented.
No mouse-drag selection, actual clipboard copy, native Find UI, screen-reader session, link navigation, giant single message, or arbitrary scrollbar dragging check.
Only relevant extension resources and read instruction/test/evidence inputs are hash-checked. This is not a claim to have hashed every file in the repository. Existing user changes were preserved.

reproducibility.allOutputs: Only build/efficiency-20261103/panel-rendering-experiment* paths. Profile removed after context.close; servers closed in nested finally.
